vulnerabilities.title: HEAP_BUFFER_OVERFLOW_SIZE_DERIVATION_FROM_CHUNK_HEADER

root_cause.description: In the write function (sub_c11 at 0xc11), the maximum write length is derived by reading the low byte of the malloc chunk size field at *(ptrs[idx]-8), then computing real_limit = chunk_size_byte - 8. For chunks allocated via calloc(0x40, 1), the chunk size is 0x51 (0x40 user data + 0x10 header + 0x1 PREV_INUSE flag). The low byte 0x51 yields real_limit = 0x51 - 8 = 0x49 = 73. When the user-supplied write_length exceeds 73, it is capped to 0x48 = 72 bytes. However, the actual user data area is only 64 bytes (0x40). The cap value 0x48 (72) exceeds the allocated user area by 8 bytes, causing an 8-byte heap buffer overflow into the next adjacent heap chunk's metadata (prev_size and size fields). The root cause is that the size limit is derived from the chunk header size field (which includes header + flags) rather than from the actual user-data allocation size, and the fallback cap 0x48 is hardcoded to a value larger than the 0x40 allocation.

affected_objects: ptrs[idx] heap chunk user data area (64 bytes / 0x40)
adjacent heap chunk prev_size field (8 bytes overflow target)
adjacent heap chunk size field (8 bytes overflow target)

attack_surface.input: write_length (scanf %d, user-controlled integer) and content (read via sub_a56)
data_flow: User selects menu option 3 (write) in main loop
sub_c11 prompts for block_index via scanf(%d) at 0xc38, stored in [rbp-0xc]
block_index validated: >= 0 (js at 0xc42) and <= 14 (cmp 0xe, jle at 0xc4a)
ptrs[block_index] loaded and checked != NULL (test rax,rax at 0xc75)
User prompted for write_length via scanf(%d) at 0xcaa, stored in [rbp-0x8]
ptrs[block_index] reloaded at 0xcd7, subtracted by 8 to point to chunk size field
Low byte of chunk size read via movzx eax, BYTE PTR [rax] at 0xcdf
Byte sign-extended via movsx eax, al at 0xce2
real_limit = chunk_size_byte - 8 computed at 0xce8, stored in [rbp-0x4]
Comparison: cmp [rbp-0x4], [rbp-0x8] (real_limit vs write_length) at 0xcef; jge 0xd09 if real_limit >= write_length
If write_length > real_limit: [rbp-0x8] set to 0x48 (72) at 0xd02
sub_a56 called with read(0, ptrs[block_index], write_length) at 0xd43
read() writes write_length bytes into 64-byte user area, overflowing by up to 8 bytes

security_check.expected: The write length should be bounded by the actual user-data allocation size (0x40 = 64 bytes) to prevent writing beyond the allocated heap chunk boundary.
security_check.actual: The write length is bounded by a value derived from the malloc chunk size field's low byte minus 8 (0x51 - 8 = 0x49 = 73), with a fallback cap of 0x48 = 72. Both 73 and 72 exceed the 64-byte user data area.
security_check.missing_or_incorrect: The size limit derivation confuses the chunk size field (which includes the 16-byte header and PREV_INUSE flag) with the user-data size. The correct limit should be the calloc allocation size (0x40 = 64). The fallback cap 0x48 is also incorrect — it should be <= 0x40.

vulnerable_operation.address: 0xd43 (call to sub_a56 which calls read at 0xa9b)
vulnerable_operation.expression: read(0, ptrs[block_index], write_length) where write_length can be up to 0x48 (72) but ptrs[block_index] points to a 0x40 (64) byte user area
vulnerable_operation.target: Heap chunk user data area of calloc(0x40, 1) allocation, overflowing 8 bytes into the next adjacent heap chunk's prev_size and size metadata fields
vulnerable_operation.size: Up to 72 bytes written into 64-byte buffer = 8-byte overflow

impact.reason: Static analysis confirms that the write path can write up to 72 bytes into a 64-byte heap allocation, producing an 8-byte overflow into the next chunk's metadata. The overflow target is the adjacent chunk's prev_size (8 bytes) and size field, which are critical heap metadata. Overwriting the size field of an adjacent chunk can corrupt the heap allocator's internal state.

The 8-byte overflow writes attacker-controlled data (from stdin read) into the next heap chunk's prev_size and size fields. Corrupting these metadata fields can cause the glibc 2.24 heap allocator (fastbin/unsortedbin, no tcache) to mishandle subsequent free/malloc operations on the affected chunk, leading to heap metadata corruption.

The overflow directly overwrites the adjacent chunk's prev_size and size fields with attacker-controlled bytes from the read() input, corrupting heap metadata that the allocator relies on for chunk boundary tracking.

evidence.description: add function calls calloc(0x40, 1) — allocates 64 bytes of user data. Confirmed: mov esi,0x1; mov edi,0x40; call calloc@plt. All heap chunks in ptrs[] are 64-byte user allocations.

Write function reads chunk size byte: sub rax,0x8 (point to chunk header); movzx eax, BYTE PTR [rax] (read only low byte of size field); movsx eax, al (sign-extend byte); sub [rbp-0x4], 0x8 (real_limit = chunk_size_byte - 8). For calloc(0x40,1): chunk size=0x51, low byte=0x51, real_limit=0x51-8=0x49=73.

Length capping logic: cmp [rbp-0x4], [rbp-0x8] (cmp real_limit, write_length); jge 0xd09 (skip if real_limit >= write_length); else mov DWORD PTR [rbp-0x8], 0x48 (set write_length = 72). The cap 0x48=72 exceeds the 64-byte user area by 8 bytes.

Final write: mov edx, [rbp-0x8] (write_length as 3rd arg); loads ptrs[block_index] into rdi; call sub_a56 which calls read(0, ptrs[idx], write_length). read() writes exactly write_length bytes with no null termination.

Derived overflow calculation: calloc(0x40,1) → user area = 64 bytes. Chunk size = 0x51 (0x40 + 0x10 header + 0x1 PREV_INUSE). Low byte = 0x51. real_limit = 0x51 - 8 = 0x49 = 73. If user supplies write_length > 73, capped to 0x48 = 72. 72 - 64 = 8 bytes overflow into next chunk's prev_size (8 bytes) and potentially size field. The overflow is into adjacent heap chunk metadata.
sub_a56 calls read(0, buf, len) directly with movsxd rdx, eax (sign-extend len to 64-bit). No null termination, no length re-validation. Reads exactly len bytes into the buffer.

verification_required: Verify the exact heap layout at runtime to confirm that the 8-byte overflow lands on the next chunk's prev_size and size fields (requires running the binary with a compatible ld/libc)
Confirm that glibc 2.24 fastbin/unsortedbin behavior allows the corrupted size field to cause exploitable heap corruption on subsequent free/malloc operations
Verify whether the overflow can be used to corrupt the size field of an adjacent chunk to enable overlapping allocations or chunk consolidation attacks

vulnerabilities.title: HEAP_INFO_LEAK_VIA_NON_NULL_TERMINATED_PUTS

root_cause.description: In the view function (sub_e0d at 0xe0d), heap content is output via puts(ptrs[block_index]). The puts() function outputs bytes until it encounters a NUL terminator. However, the write path (sub_c11 → sub_a56 → read()) does not null-terminate the data written to the heap buffer. Since calloc zero-initializes the buffer, the first write of N bytes leaves bytes N through 63 as NUL, so puts stops at byte N. But if the heap chunk's content is fully filled (e.g., 64 bytes of non-NUL data written via a 0x40-length write, or if the overflow writes non-NUL bytes into adjacent metadata), puts will read past the intended content boundary into adjacent heap metadata or adjacent chunk data until a NUL byte is found. This can leak heap metadata (chunk size, fd/bk pointers from freed chunks) and adjacent heap content.

affected_objects: adjacent heap chunk metadata (fd/bk pointers, size fields)

data_flow: User selects menu option 2 (view) in main loop
sub_e0d prompts for block_index via sub_aca (read 0x40 bytes, atoi) at 0xe21
block_index validated: >= 0 (js at 0xe37) and <= 14 (cmp 0xe, jle at 0xe3d)
ptrs[block_index] loaded and checked != NULL (test rax,rax at 0xe65)
Chunk size byte read from ptr-8 at 0xe90-0xe9a (but NOT used for output length limiting)
puts(ptrs[block_index]) called at 0xeb8 — outputs heap content as a C string until NUL

security_check.expected: The view function should limit output to the actual content length or the allocation size, preventing reads beyond the chunk boundary.
security_check.actual: The view function reads the chunk size byte from ptr-8 (at 0xe90-0xe9a) but does not use it to limit the puts() output. puts() reads until NUL with no length bound.
security_check.missing_or_incorrect: No length-bounded output function (e.g., write with explicit length) is used. The chunk size byte is read but discarded — it does not constrain the output.

vulnerable_operation.expression: puts(ptrs[block_index]) — outputs heap content as C string with no length bound
vulnerable_operation.target: Heap chunk user data and potentially adjacent heap metadata/data beyond the chunk boundary

impact.reason: If a heap chunk is filled with non-NUL data (up to 64 bytes via write, or if the 8-byte overflow from BUG-001 writes non-NUL bytes into adjacent metadata), puts() will read past the chunk boundary into adjacent heap metadata. In glibc 2.24, freed chunks in fastbins/unsortedbins contain fd/bk pointers (heap addresses and potentially libc addresses). If a freed chunk is adjacent to a viewed chunk and contains non-NUL pointer data, puts() may leak these addresses. Additionally, if the overflow from BUG-001 corrupts the adjacent chunk's size field with non-NUL bytes, puts() on the overflowed chunk will read into the adjacent chunk's metadata.

evidence.description: View function reads chunk size byte at 0xe90 (sub rax,0x8; movzx eax, BYTE PTR [rax]; movsx eax, al) and stores in [rbp-0x4] at 0xe9a, but this value is never used to limit output. At 0xeb8, puts(ptrs[block_index]) is called with no length constraint.
The write path uses read(0, buf, len) which does not null-terminate the buffer. Data written to heap chunks has no guaranteed NUL terminator at the end of written content.

calloc zero-initializes buffers, so initially puts() stops at the first unwritten byte. But if a chunk is fully filled with 64 non-NUL bytes (write_length=0x40), or if BUG-001's overflow writes non-NUL bytes into the adjacent chunk's prev_size/size fields, puts() will read past the 64-byte boundary into adjacent heap metadata, potentially leaking heap/libc addresses from freed chunk fd/bk pointers.

verification_required: Verify at runtime that filling a chunk with 64 non-NUL bytes causes puts() to read into adjacent metadata
Confirm whether adjacent freed chunks contain non-NUL pointer data that would be leaked by puts()
Verify whether the 8-byte overflow from BUG-001 can be arranged to place non-NUL bytes that bridge two chunks for a puts() read-past-boundary

non_vulnerabilities.description: The remove function calls free(ptrs[block_index]) and then immediately sets ptrs[block_index] = NULL (at 0xe02: mov QWORD PTR [rdx+rax*1], 0x0).
non_vulnerabilities.reason: The pointer is properly NULLed after free, preventing use-after-free via the ptrs[] array. Subsequent view/write/remove operations check ptrs[idx] != NULL before use, so a freed-and-NULLed slot cannot be accessed. No UAF in the remove function itself.

non_vulnerabilities.description: block_index is validated with test eax,eax; js (checks >= 0, signed) and cmp eax,0xe; jle (checks <= 14, signed). The ptrs[] array has 15 elements (indices 0-14).
non_vulnerabilities.reason: The index bounds check is correct: 0 <= block_index <= 14 matches the array bounds. The signed comparison is appropriate here because scanf(%d) produces a signed int, and both the lower bound (js = jump if sign/negative) and upper bound (cmp 0xe, jle) correctly reject out-of-range values. No OOB via index.

non_vulnerabilities.function: sub_d4b (remove, 0xd4b) and sub_e0d (view, 0xe0d) — block_index bounds check
non_vulnerabilities.description: Both functions validate block_index with the same pattern: cmp [rbp-0x4],0x0; js (>= 0) and cmp [rbp-0x4],0xe; jle (<= 14).
non_vulnerabilities.reason: Index bounds checks are correct and consistent with the ptrs[] array size of 15 elements. No OOB via index in remove or view.

non_vulnerabilities.description: readint reads 0x40 bytes into a stack buffer of 0x50 bytes (with stack canary protection), then calls atoi().
non_vulnerabilities.reason: The stack buffer (0x50 = 80 bytes) is larger than the read length (0x40 = 64 bytes), so no stack buffer overflow. Stack canary is present and checked at 0xb65-0xb74. atoi() return is used as a signed int for index validation.
